sentences.zh: 廣平公盛 陽州公永樂 弟長弼 襄樂王顯國 上洛王思宗 子元海 弟思好 平秦王歸彥 武興王普 長樂太守靈山 嗣子伏護

translations.literal: Duke Sheng of Guangping; Duke Yongle of Yangzhou; younger brother Changbi; Prince Xianguo of Xiangle; Prince Sigu of Shangluo; son Yuanhai; younger brother Sihao; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin; Prince Pu of Wuxing; Lingshan, Governor of Changle; successor son Fuhu
translations.idiomatic: Duke Sheng of Guangping; Duke Yongle of Yangzhou; younger brother Changbi; Prince Xianguo of Xiangle; Prince Sigu of Shangluo; son Yuanhai; younger brother Sihao; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin; Prince Pu of Wuxing; Lingshan, Governor of Changle; successor son Fuhu

sentences.zh: 廣平公盛，神武從叔祖也。

translations.literal: Duke Sheng of Guangping was a great-uncle of the Grand Ancestor on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Sheng of Guangping was a great-uncle of Gao Huan on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 寬厚有長者風。

translations.literal: Generous and mild, he had the bearing of an elder of worth.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and mild, he had the bearing of an elder of worth.

sentences.zh: 神武起兵於信都，以盛為中軍大都督，封廣平郡公。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised troops at Xindu, he made Sheng Grand Commander of the Center Army and enfeoffed him Duke of Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised troops at Xindu, he made Sheng grand commander of the center army and enfeoffed him duke of Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 歷位司徒、太尉。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Minister of Works and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to minister of works and grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 天平三年，薨於位。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianping, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞，太尉、太師、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Commandant, Grand Preceptor, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand commandant, grand preceptor, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄子子瑗嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, he made his elder brother's son Ziyuan his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, he made his elder brother's son Ziyuan his heir.

sentences.zh: 天保初，改封平昌王，卒於魏尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to Prince of Pingchang; he died while serving as Governor of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to prince of Pingchang; he died while serving as governor of Wei.

sentences.zh: 陽州公永樂，神武從祖兄子也。

translations.literal: Duke Yongle of Yangzhou was the son of the Grand Ancestor's father's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yongle of Yangzhou was the son of Gao Huan's father's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，封陽州縣伯，進爵為公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangzhou County and his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang, he was enfeoffed baron of Yangzhou County and his rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 累遷北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Governor of Beiyu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to governor of Beiyu Province.

sentences.zh: 河陰之戰，司徒高昂失利退。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Heyin, Minister of Works Gao Ang suffered defeat and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Heyin, Minister of Works Gao Ang suffered defeat and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 永樂守河陽南城，昂走趣城，西軍追者將至，永樂不開門，昂遂為西軍所擒。

translations.literal: Yongle held the southern city of Heyang; Ang fled toward the city, and as the Western army's pursuers were about to arrive, Yongle would not open the gate — Ang was thereupon captured by the Western army.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle held the southern city of Heyang; Ang fled toward the city, and as the Western army's pursuers were about to arrive, Yongle would not open the gate — Ang was thereupon captured by the Western army.

sentences.zh: 神武大怒，杖之二百。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor was furious and had him beaten two hundred strokes with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was furious and had him beaten two hundred strokes with the staff.

sentences.zh: 後罷豫州，家產不立。

translations.literal: Later he was removed from Yu Province, and his household estate was not established.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was removed from Yu Province, and his household estate was not established.

sentences.zh: 神武問其故，對曰：「裴監為長史，辛公正為別駕，受王委寄，斗酒只雞不入。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor asked the reason; he replied, "Pei Jian served as Chief Administrator, and Xin Gongzheng as Vice Director — entrusted by the prince, they would not accept so much as a cup of wine or a chicken.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan asked the reason; he replied, "Pei Jian served as chief administrator, and Xin Gongzheng as vice director — entrusted by the prince, they would not accept so much as a cup of wine or a chicken.

sentences.zh: 」神武乃以永樂為濟州，仍以監、公正為長史、別駕。

translations.literal: " The Grand Ancestor thereupon made Yongle Governor of Ji Province and again appointed Jian and Gongzheng as Chief Administrator and Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan thereupon made Yongle governor of Ji Province and again appointed Jian and Gongzheng as chief administrator and vice director.

sentences.zh: 謂永樂曰：「爾勿大貪，小小義取莫復畏。

translations.literal: He said to Yongle, "Do not be too greedy — take a little in propriety and need not fear again.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Yongle, "Do not be too greedy — take a little in propriety and need not fear again.

sentences.zh: 」永樂至州，監、公正諫不見聽，以狀啟神武。

translations.literal: " When Yongle reached the province, Jian and Gongzheng remonstrated but were not heeded; they submitted a report to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yongle reached the province, Jian and Gongzheng remonstrated but were not heeded; they submitted a report to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武封啟以示永樂。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor sealed the report and showed it to Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sealed the report and showed it to Yongle.

sentences.zh: 然後知二人清直，並擢用之。

translations.literal: Only then did he know the two men were upright and incorrupt; both were promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he know the two men were upright and incorrupt; both were promoted and employed.

sentences.zh: 永樂卒於州。

translations.literal: Yongle died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle died in the province.

sentences.zh: 贈太師、太尉、錄尚書事，諡曰武昭。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand preceptor, grand commandant, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhao.

sentences.zh: 無子，從兄思宗以第二子孝緒為後，襲爵。

translations.literal: Having no son, his elder cousin Sigu made his second son Xiaoxu his successor to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, his elder cousin Sigu made his second son Xiaoxu his successor to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 天保初，改封脩城郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to Prince of Xiucheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to prince of Xiucheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永樂弟長弼，小名阿伽。

translations.literal: Yongle's younger brother Changbi had the childhood name A'jia.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle's younger brother Changbi had the childhood name A'jia.

sentences.zh: 性粗武，出入城市，好毆擊行路，時人皆呼為阿伽郎君。

translations.literal: By nature coarse and martial, going in and out of the city he liked to beat passersby on the road; people at the time all called him Lord A'jia.
translations.idiomatic: By nature coarse and martial, going in and out of the city he liked to beat passersby on the road; people at the time all called him Lord A'jia.

sentences.zh: 以宗室封廣武王。

translations.literal: As a member of the imperial clan he was enfeoffed Prince of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the imperial clan he was enfeoffed prince of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 時有天恩道人，至兇暴，橫行閭肆，後入長弼黨，專以鬬為事。

translations.literal: At that time there was a Daoist monk named Tian'en, extremely violent, who rampaged through the lanes and marketplaces; later he joined Changbi's faction and devoted himself entirely to brawling.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a Daoist monk named Tian'en, extremely violent, who rampaged through the lanes and marketplaces; later he joined Changbi's faction and devoted himself entirely to brawling.

sentences.zh: 文宣並收掩付獄，天恩黨十餘人皆棄市，長弼鞭一百。

translations.literal: Wenxuan arrested and imprisoned them all; more than ten of Tian'en's followers were executed in the marketplace, and Changbi was flogged one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang arrested and imprisoned them all; more than ten of Tian'en's followers were executed in the marketplace, and Changbi was flogged one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 尋為南營州刺史，在州無故自驚走，叛亡入突厥，竟不知死所。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made Governor of Southern Ying Province; in the province, for no reason he panicked and fled, rebelled, and entered the Turks — in the end no one knew where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made governor of Southern Ying Province; in the province, for no reason he panicked and fled, rebelled, and entered the Turks — in the end no one knew where he died.

sentences.zh: 上洛王思宗，神武從子也。

translations.literal: Prince Sigu of Shangluo was a nephew of the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sigu of Shangluo was a nephew of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 性寬和，頗有武幹。

translations.literal: By nature generous and mild, he possessed considerable martial ability.
translations.idiomatic: By nature generous and mild, he possessed considerable martial ability.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封上洛郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangluo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed prince of Shangluo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 歷位司空、太傅。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Minister of Works and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to minister of works and grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 薨於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子元海，累遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Yuanhai rose in succession to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanhai rose in succession to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 願處山林，脩行釋典。

translations.literal: He wished to dwell in mountain forests and cultivate the Buddhist canon.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to dwell in mountain forests and cultivate the Buddhist canon.

sentences.zh: 文宣許之。

translations.literal: Wenxuan granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang granted his request.

sentences.zh: 乃入林慮山，經二年，絕棄人事，志不能固，啟求歸。

translations.literal: He then entered Mount Linlu, and for two years utterly abandoned human affairs; his resolve could not hold firm, and he petitioned asking to return.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered Mount Linlu, and for two years utterly abandoned human affairs; his resolve could not hold firm, and he petitioned asking to return.

sentences.zh: 徵復本任，便縱酒肆情，廣納姬侍。

translations.literal: Summoned back to his original post, he thereupon gave himself to wine and unrestrained pleasure, widely taking concubines and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned back to his original post, he thereupon gave himself to wine and unrestrained pleasure, widely taking concubines and attendants.

sentences.zh: 又除領軍，器小志大，頗以智謀自許。

translations.literal: He was also made Commander of the Army; small in capacity but great in ambition, he rather prided himself on clever stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made commander of the army; small in capacity but great in ambition, he rather prided himself on clever stratagems.

sentences.zh: 皇建末，孝昭幸晉陽，武成居守，元海以散騎常侍留典機密。

translations.literal: At the end of the Huangjian era, Xiaozhao visited Jinyang while Wucheng remained on guard; Yuanhai, as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, stayed behind to manage confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Huangjian era, Gao Yan visited Jinyang while Gao Zhan remained on guard; Yuanhai, as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, stayed behind to manage confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 初孝昭之誅楊愔等，謂武成云：「事成，以爾為皇太弟。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao first executed Yang Yin and the others, he had told Wucheng, "When the affair succeeds, I will make you Imperial Younger Brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan first executed Yang Yin and the others, he had told Gao Zhan, "When the affair succeeds, I will make you imperial younger brother.

sentences.zh: 」及踐祚，乃使武成在鄴主兵，立子百年為皇太子，武成甚不平。

translations.literal: " When he ascended the throne, he made Wucheng hold troops at Ye and established his son Bainian as crown prince — Wucheng was very discontent.
translations.idiomatic: " When he ascended the throne, he made Gao Zhan hold troops at Ye and established his son Bainian as crown prince — Gao Zhan was very discontent.

sentences.zh: 先是，恒留濟南於鄴，除領軍厙狄伏連為幽州刺史，以斛律豐樂為領軍，以分武成之權。

translations.literal: Before this, the Prince of Ji'nan had always been kept at Ye; Kudi Fulian was made Governor of You Province, and Hulu Fengle was made Commander of the Army — both to divide Wucheng's power.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the Prince of Ji'nan had always been kept at Ye; Kudi Fulian was made governor of You Province, and Hulu Fengle was made commander of the army — both to divide Gao Zhan's power.

sentences.zh: 武成留伏連而不聽豐樂視事。

translations.literal: Wucheng kept Fulian but would not allow Fengle to assume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan kept Fulian but would not allow Fengle to assume his duties.

sentences.zh: 乃與河南王孝瑜偽獵，謀於野，暗乃歸。

translations.literal: He then joined Prince Xiaoyu of Henan in a feigned hunt, plotting in the wild, and returned only after dark.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Prince Xiaoyu of Henan in a feigned hunt, plotting in the wild, and returned only after dark.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠云：「中興寺內白鳧翁，四方側聽聲雍雍，道人聞之夜打鐘。

translations.literal: Before this a children's rhyme said, "At Zhongxing Temple, a white duck old man — from the four quarters they listen, the sound harmonious; the Daoist hears it and at night strikes the bell.
translations.idiomatic: Before this a children's rhyme said, "At Zhongxing Temple, a white duck old man — from the four quarters they listen, the sound harmonious; the Daoist hears it and at night strikes the bell.

sentences.zh: 」時丞相府在北城中，卽舊中興寺也。

translations.literal: " At that time the chancellor's headquarters was in the northern city — that is, the old Zhongxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the chancellor's headquarters was in the northern city — that is, the old Zhongxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 鳧翁，謂雄雞，蓋指武成小字步落稽也。

translations.literal: "Duck old man" means rooster — it pointed to Wucheng's childhood name Buluoqi.
translations.idiomatic: "Duck old man" means rooster — it pointed to Gao Zhan's childhood name Buluoqi.

sentences.zh: 道人，濟南王小名。

translations.literal: "The Daoist" was the Prince of Ji'nan's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: "The Daoist" was the Prince of Ji'nan's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 打鐘，言將被擊也。

translations.literal: "Strikes the bell" meant he would be beaten.
translations.idiomatic: "Strikes the bell" meant he would be beaten.

sentences.zh: 旣而太史奏言北城有天子氣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the court astrologer memorialized that there was an emperor's aura in the northern city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the court astrologer memorialized that there was an emperor's aura in the northern city.

sentences.zh: 昭帝以為濟南應之，乃使平秦王歸彥之鄴，迎濟南赴幷州。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao thought the Prince of Ji'nan corresponded to it; he therefore sent Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to Ye to welcome the Prince of Ji'nan to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan thought the Prince of Ji'nan corresponded to it; he therefore sent Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to Ye to welcome the Prince of Ji'nan to Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 武成先咨元海，並問自安之計。

translations.literal: Wucheng first consulted Yuanhai and also asked for a plan to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan first consulted Yuanhai and also asked for a plan to secure himself.

sentences.zh: 元海曰：「皇太后萬福，至尊孝性非常，殿下不須別慮。

translations.literal: Yuanhai said, "The Empress Dowager enjoys boundless fortune; the emperor's filial nature is extraordinary — Your Highness need not worry otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai said, "The Empress Dowager enjoys boundless fortune; the emperor's filial nature is extraordinary — Your Highness need not worry otherwise.

sentences.zh: 」武成曰：「豈我推誠之意耶？

translations.literal: " Wucheng said, "Is this truly the meaning of my open-hearted sincerity?
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Zhan said, "Is this truly the meaning of my open-hearted sincerity?

sentences.zh: 」元海乞還省一夜思之。

translations.literal: " Yuanhai asked to return to his quarters and think on it one night.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanhai asked to return to his quarters and think on it one night.

sentences.zh: 武成卽留元海後堂。

translations.literal: Wucheng kept Yuanhai in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan kept Yuanhai in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 元海達旦不眠，唯繞床徐步。

translations.literal: Yuanhai went all night without sleep, only pacing slowly around the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai went all night without sleep, only pacing slowly around the bed.

sentences.zh: 夜漏未曙，武成遽出，曰：「神算如何？

translations.literal: Before dawn Wucheng hurried out and said, "What is your divine calculation?
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn Gao Zhan hurried out and said, "What is your divine calculation?

sentences.zh: 」答云：「夜中得三策，恐不堪用耳。

translations.literal: " He answered, "In the night I obtained three stratagems — I fear they may not be usable.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "In the night I obtained three stratagems — I fear they may not be usable.

sentences.zh: 」因說梁孝王懼誅入關事，請乘數騎入晉陽，先見太后求哀，後見主上，請去兵權，以死為限，求不干朝政，必保太山之安。

translations.literal: " He then spoke of Prince Xiao of Liang, who fearing execution entered the passes, and proposed that with a few horsemen he enter Jinyang, first see the Empress Dowager and beg mercy, then see the sovereign and request removal of military authority, taking death as his limit and seeking not to interfere in court governance — he would surely preserve the security of Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: " He then spoke of Prince Xiao of Liang, who fearing execution entered the passes, and proposed that with a few horsemen he enter Jinyang, first see the Empress Dowager and beg mercy, then see the sovereign and request removal of military authority, taking death as his limit and seeking not to interfere in court governance — he would surely preserve the security of Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 此上策也。

translations.literal: This was the upper stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: This was the upper stratagem.

sentences.zh: 若不然，當具表，云「『威權大盛，恐取謗衆口』，請青、齊二州刺史。

translations.literal: If not, he should submit a memorial stating, "'My authority and power are too great; I fear I will draw slander from the multitude' — and request the governorships of Qing and Qi Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: If not, he should submit a memorial stating, "'My authority and power are too great; I fear I will draw slander from the multitude' — and request the governorships of Qing and Qi Provinces.

sentences.zh: 沉靜自居，必不招物議。

translations.literal: Dwelling in quiet and keeping to himself, he would surely not invite public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in quiet and keeping to himself, he would surely not invite public criticism.

sentences.zh: 此中策也。

translations.literal: This was the middle stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: This was the middle stratagem.

sentences.zh: 」更問下策曰：「發言卽恐族誅。

translations.literal: " When asked further about the lower stratagem he said, "To speak would mean immediate execution of the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: " When asked further about the lower stratagem he said, "To speak would mean immediate execution of the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 」因逼之，答曰：「濟南世嫡，主上假太后令而奪之。

translations.literal: " Pressed, he answered, "The Prince of Ji'nan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne through the Empress Dowager's order.
translations.idiomatic: " Pressed, he answered, "The Prince of Ji'nan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne through the Empress Dowager's order.

sentences.zh: 今集文武，示以此勑，執豐樂，斬歸彥，尊濟南，號令天下，以順討逆，此萬世一時也。

translations.literal: Now gather the civil and military officials, display this edict, seize Fengle, behead Guiyan, honor the Prince of Ji'nan, and proclaim to the realm — with righteousness to punish rebellion, this would be a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Now gather the civil and military officials, display this edict, seize Fengle, behead Guiyan, honor the Prince of Ji'nan, and proclaim to the realm — with righteousness to punish rebellion, this would be a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity.

sentences.zh: 」武成大悅，狐疑，竟未能用。

translations.literal: " Wucheng was greatly pleased but hesitated, and in the end could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Zhan was greatly pleased but hesitated, and in the end could not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 乃使鄭道謙卜之，皆曰：「不利舉事，靜則吉。

translations.literal: He then had Zheng Daoqian perform divination; all said, "It is unfavorable to act; quiet brings good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Zheng Daoqian perform divination; all said, "It is unfavorable to act; quiet brings good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」又召曹魏祖，問之國事。

translations.literal: " He also summoned Cao Weizu and questioned him on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He also summoned Cao Weizu and questioned him on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「當有大凶。

translations.literal: He replied, "There will be great misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "There will be great misfortune.

sentences.zh: 」又時有林慮令姓潘，知占候，密謂武成曰：「宮車當晏駕，殿下為天下主。

translations.literal: " At that time the Magistrate of Linlu, surnamed Pan, knew divination and omens; he secretly told Wucheng, "The imperial carriage will break at dusk — Your Highness will be sovereign of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the Magistrate of Linlu, surnamed Pan, knew divination and omens; he secretly told Gao Zhan, "The imperial carriage will break at dusk — Your Highness will be sovereign of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」武成拘之於內以候之。

translations.literal: " Wucheng detained him inside to wait for the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Zhan detained him inside to wait for the outcome.

sentences.zh: 又令巫覡卜之，多云不須舉兵，自有大慶。

translations.literal: He also had shamans perform divination; most said there was no need to raise troops — great good fortune would come of itself.
translations.idiomatic: He also had shamans perform divination; most said there was no need to raise troops — great good fortune would come of itself.

sentences.zh: 武成乃奉詔，令數百騎送濟南於晉陽。

translations.literal: Wucheng thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Ji'nan to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Ji'nan to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及孝昭崩，武成卽位，除元海侍中、開府儀同三司、太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao died and Wucheng ascended the throne, Yuanhai was made Palace Attendant, Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan died and Gao Zhan ascended the throne, Yuanhai was made palace attendant, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and grand tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 河清二年，元海為和士開所譖，被捶馬鞭六十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heqing, Yuanhai was slandered by He Shikai and was beaten sixty strokes with the horsewhip.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Heqing, Yuanhai was slandered by He Shikai and was beaten sixty strokes with the horsewhip.

sentences.zh: 責云：「爾在鄴城，說我以弟反兄，幾許不義！

translations.literal: He was rebuked, "You at Ye told me to rebel as younger brother against elder brother — how many acts of unrighteousness were there!
translations.idiomatic: He was rebuked, "You at Ye told me to rebel as younger brother against elder brother — how many acts of unrighteousness were there!

sentences.zh: 鄴城兵馬抗幷州，幾許無智！

translations.literal: Ye's troops and horses resisting Bing Province — how many acts of folly were there!
translations.idiomatic: Ye's troops and horses resisting Bing Province — how many acts of folly were there!

sentences.zh: 不義無智，若為可使？

translations.literal: Unrighteous and foolish — how could you be employed?
translations.idiomatic: Unrighteous and foolish — how could you be employed?

sentences.zh: 」出為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: " He was sent out as Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: " He was sent out as governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 元海後妻，陸太姬甥也，故尋被追任使。

translations.literal: Yuanhai's later wife was a niece of Empress Dowager Lu; for this reason he was soon recalled and given employment again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai's later wife was a niece of Empress Dowager Lu; for this reason he was soon recalled and given employment again.

sentences.zh: 武平中，與祖珽共執朝政。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era he jointly held court governance with Zu Ting.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuping era he jointly held court governance with Zu Ting.

sentences.zh: 元海多以太姬密語告珽。

translations.literal: Yuanhai often reported the Empress Dowager's confidential words to Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai often reported the Empress Dowager's confidential words to Ting.

sentences.zh: 珽求領軍，元海不可，珽乃以其所告報太姬。

translations.literal: Ting sought the post of Commander of the Army; Yuanhai would not agree — Ting thereupon reported what Yuanhai had told him to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Ting sought the post of commander of the army; Yuanhai would not agree — Ting thereupon reported what Yuanhai had told him to the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 姬怒，出元海為鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was angry and sent Yuanhai out as Governor of Zheng Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was angry and sent Yuanhai out as governor of Zheng Province.

sentences.zh: 鄴城將敗，徵為尚書令。

translations.literal: When Ye was about to fall, he was summoned and made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye was about to fall, he was summoned and made director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 周建德七年，於鄴城謀逆，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, at Ye he plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, at Ye he plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 元海好亂樂禍，然詐仁慈，不飲灑啖肉。

translations.literal: Yuanhai loved disorder and delighted in calamity, yet feigned benevolence — he did not drink wine or eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai loved disorder and delighted in calamity, yet feigned benevolence — he did not drink wine or eat meat.

sentences.zh: 文宣天保末年敬信內法，乃至宗廟不血食，皆元海所謀。

translations.literal: In the last years of Tianbao, Wenxuan revered and believed in the inner Buddhist law, even to the point that the ancestral temple had no blood offerings — all was Yuanhai's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Tianbao, Gao Yang revered and believed in the inner Buddhist law, even to the point that the ancestral temple had no blood offerings — all was Yuanhai's counsel.

sentences.zh: 及為右僕射，又說後主禁屠宰，斷酤酒。

translations.literal: When he was Right Vice Minister, he again persuaded the Last Emperor to forbid slaughter and cut off the sale of wine.
translations.idiomatic: When he was right vice minister, he again persuaded the Last Emperor to forbid slaughter and cut off the sale of wine.

sentences.zh: 然本心非靖，故終致覆敗。

translations.literal: Yet his heart was not truly at peace — therefore in the end he brought on ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his heart was not truly at peace — therefore in the end he brought on ruin.

sentences.zh: 思宗弟思好。

translations.literal: Sigu's younger brother Sihao.
translations.idiomatic: Sigu's younger brother Sihao.

sentences.zh: 思好本浩氏子也，思宗養以為弟，遇之甚薄。

translations.literal: Sihao was originally a son of the Hao clan; Sigu raised him as a younger brother but treated him very poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Sihao was originally a son of the Hao clan; Sigu raised him as a younger brother but treated him very poorly.

sentences.zh: 少以騎射事文襄。

translations.literal: In youth he served the Imperial Founder in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Gao Cheng in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 及文宣受命，為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan received the Mandate, Sihao was made Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan took the throne, Sihao was made grand general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 本名思孝，天保五年，討蠕蠕，文宣悅其驍勇，謂曰：「爾擊賊如鶻入鴉群，宜思好事。

translations.literal: His original name was Sixiao. In the fifth year of Tianbao, campaigning against the Rouran, Wenxuan was pleased with his fierce valor and said: "You strike the enemy like a goshawk among crows — you ought to think of good deeds.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Sixiao. In the fifth year of Tianbao, on campaign against the Rouran, Wenxuan delighted in his fierce bravery and said, "You strike the enemy like a goshawk among crows — think on deeds worthy of that gift.

sentences.zh: 」故改名焉。

translations.literal: " Hence he was renamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hence his name was changed.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書令、朔州道行臺、朔州刺史、開府、南安王，甚得邊朔人心。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Director of the Masters of Writing, Field Headquarters of the Shuozhou Circuit, Governor of Shuozhou, opening-establishment, and Prince of Nan'an — and won the hearts of the northern frontier greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to director of the Masters of Writing, field headquarters of the Shuozhou circuit, governor of Shuozhou, opening-establishment honors, and Prince of Nan'an — and won deep loyalty on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 後主時，斫骨光弁奉使至州，思好迎之甚謹，光弁倨敖，思好因心銜恨。

translations.literal: In the time of the Later Lord, Zhuogu Guangbian came on mission to the province; Sihao received him with great courtesy, but Guangbian was arrogant and haughty — Sihao therefore nursed resentment in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Lord, Zhuogu Guangbian came to the province on mission. Sihao received him with scrupulous courtesy; Guangbian repaid him with arrogance — and Sihao nursed the insult in silence.

sentences.zh: 武平五年，遂舉兵反。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wuping, he thereupon raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wuping he rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 與幷州諸貴書曰：「主上少長深宮，未辨人之情偽，昵近兇狡，疏遠忠良。

translations.literal: He wrote to the nobles of Bing Province: "Our lord grew up deep in the palace and cannot distinguish true from false in men; he draws close to the vicious and cunning and keeps the loyal and good at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the nobles of Bing Province: "Our lord was reared deep in the palace and cannot tell sincerity from deceit. He cleaves to the vicious and shuns the loyal.

sentences.zh: 遂使刀鋸刑餘，貴溢軒階，商胡醜類，擅權帷幄，剝削生靈，劫掠朝市。

translations.literal: Thus eunuchs mutilated by blade and saw overflow the steps of the hall; vile merchant-Hu grasp power within the curtains, stripping the living and plundering the markets of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs mutilated by blade and saw now crowd the palace steps; foul merchant-adventurers hold the reins within the curtains — stripping the people bare and pillaging the court itself.

sentences.zh: 闇於聽受，專行忍害。

translations.literal: Dull in hearing and accepting counsel, he devotes himself to cruel harm.
translations.idiomatic: Deaf to remonstrance, he delights in cruelty.

sentences.zh: 幽母深宮，無復人子之禮；

translations.literal: He shuts his mother deep in the palace and no longer keeps a son's rites;
translations.idiomatic: He has locked his mother away in the inner palace and cast off a son's duty;

sentences.zh: 二弟殘戮，頓絕孔懷之義。

translations.literal: his two younger brothers were slaughtered — the bond of flesh and bone was severed at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: his two younger brothers were butchered — the bond of flesh and blood cut off in a stroke.

sentences.zh: 仍縱子立奪馬於東門，光弁擎鷹於西市，駮龍得儀同之號，逍遙受郡君之名，犬馬班位，榮冠軒冕。

translations.literal: He still indulges Zili in seizing horses at the eastern gate, Guangbian in carrying falcons at the western market — Bolo receives the title Equal in Protocol, Xiaoyao the name Lady of the Commandery; dogs and horses take rank alongside men, their glory topping the court caps and sashes.
translations.idiomatic: He indulges Zili seizing horses at the eastern gate, Guangbian strutting with falcons at the western market — Bolo granted protocol equal to princes, Xiaoyao styled lady of a commandery. Dogs and horses take rank beside men; their glory outshines court caps and robes.

sentences.zh: 人不堪役，思長亂階。

translations.literal: The people cannot bear the burdens; they long for chaos to end.
translations.idiomatic: The people buckle under their burdens and pray for an end to this disorder.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王叡實曰宗英，社稷惟寄，左丞相斛律明月，世為元輔，威著鄰國，無罪無辜，奄見誅殄。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui is truly the clan's flower — the altars rest upon him alone. Left Chancellor Hulü Guang mingled the moon, for generations a chief minister, his might famed among neighboring states — yet innocent of guilt, he was suddenly put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui is truly the flower of the clan — upon him alone the altars rest. Left Chancellor Hulü Guang mingled the moon, chief minister through generations, his renown ringing in every neighboring realm — and yet, guiltless, he was suddenly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 孤旣忝預皇枝，實蒙殊獎，今便擁率義兵，指除君側之害。

translations.literal: I, unworthy though I am to share the imperial branch, have truly received extraordinary favor — now I shall lead righteous troops to strike down the harm at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy as I am of the imperial branch, I have nonetheless received extraordinary favor. Today I lead righteous troops to purge the evil at our lord's side.

sentences.zh: 幸悉此懷，無致疑惑。

translations.literal: I pray you understand this heart and harbor no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Know my heart in this, and lend no ear to doubt.

sentences.zh: 」行臺郎王行思之辭也。

translations.literal: " — the words of Field Headquarters Attendant Wang Xingsi.
translations.idiomatic: " — penned by field headquarters attendant Wang Xingsi.

sentences.zh: 思好至陽曲，自號大丞相，置百官，以行臺左丞王尚之為長史。

translations.literal: Sihao reached Yangqu, styled himself Grand Chancellor, set up all the hundred officials, and made Left Assistant of the Field Headquarters Wang Shangzhi his chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Sihao reached Yangqu and styled himself grand chancellor. He set up a full bureaucracy and made left assistant of the field headquarters Wang Shangzhi his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 武衛趙海在晉陽掌兵，時倉卒不暇奏，矯詔發兵拒之。

translations.literal: Guard General Zhao Hai held troops at Jinyang; pressed for time and unable to memorialize, he forged an edict and mobilized troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Guard general Zhao Hai held the soldiers at Jinyang. With no time to report upward, he forged an edict and mobilized the troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 軍士皆曰：「南安王來，我輩唯須唱萬歲奉迎耳。

translations.literal: The soldiers all said: "The Prince of Nan'an is coming — we need only shout ten thousand years and welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers said among themselves, "Prince of Nan'an is coming — we need only shout 'ten thousand years!' and welcome him.

sentences.zh: 」帝聞變，使唐邕、莫多婁敬顯、劉桃枝、中領軍厙狄士文馳之晉陽，帝勒兵續進。

translations.literal: " The emperor heard of the uprising and sent Tang Yong, Moduolou Jingxian, Liu Taozhi, and Central Army Commander Kudi Shiwen galloping to Jinyang; the emperor himself led troops and followed after.
translations.idiomatic: " Learning of the revolt, the emperor sent Tang Yong, Moduolou Jingxian, Liu Taozhi, and central army commander Kudi Shiwen racing to Jinyang, while he himself led troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 思好軍敗，與行思投水而死。

translations.literal: Sihao's army was defeated; he and Xingsi threw themselves into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sihao's army collapsed. He and Xingsi cast themselves into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 其麾下二千人，桃枝圍之，且殺且招，終不降以至盡。

translations.literal: His two thousand followers — Taozhi besieged them, killing and summoning by turns; in the end none surrendered, and all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Taozhi surrounded his two thousand followers, killing and calling them to surrender in turn. None yielded, and all were killed to the last man.

sentences.zh: 時帝在道，叱奴世安自晉陽送露布於平都，遇斛斯孝卿。

translations.literal: The emperor was on the road; Chinu Shi'an carried the victory bulletin from Jinyang toward Pingdu and encountered Husixiao Xiaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still on the march when Chinu Shi'an set out from Jinyang bearing the victory bulletin toward Pingdu — and met Husixiao Xiaoqing on the way.

sentences.zh: 孝卿誘使食，因馳詣行宮，叫已了。

translations.literal: Xiaoqing tempted him to eat, then galloped on to the traveling palace and cried out that all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoqing lured him to sit and eat, then raced ahead to the traveling palace and cried out that the matter was finished.

sentences.zh: 帝大歡，左右呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced greatly; those at his side shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed; his attendants shouted "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 良久，世安乃以狀自陳。

translations.literal: After a long while Shi'an at last made his report of what had occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval did Shi'an arrive and explain what had happened.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「告示何物事，乃得坐食。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What manner of victory bulletin is this, that you could sit down and eat?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What sort of bulletin permits a man to stop and dine?

sentences.zh: 」於是賞孝卿而免世安罪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he rewarded Xiaoqing and pardoned Shi'an's offense.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded Xiaoqing and pardoned Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 暴思好屍七日，然後屠剝焚之，烹尚之於鄴市，令內參射其妃於宮內，仍火焚殺之。

translations.literal: Sihao's corpse was displayed for seven days, then flayed, butchered, and burned; Shangzhi was boiled alive at the Ye market; palace eunuchs were ordered to shoot Sihao's consort within the palace, then burn her to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sihao's corpse was put on display seven days, then butchered, skinned, and burned. Shangzhi was boiled alive in the Ye market. Palace eunuchs were told to shoot Sihao's consort inside the palace — then burn what remained.

sentences.zh: 思好反前五旬，有人告其謀反。

translations.literal: Fifty days before Sihao's rebellion someone reported his plot.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty days before the revolt, someone denounced Sihao for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 韓長鸞女適思好子，故奏有人誣告諸貴，事相擾動，不殺無以息後，乃斬之。

translations.literal: Han Changluan's daughter was married to Sihao's son — he therefore memorialized that someone was slandering the nobles, that the affair was stirring disturbance, and that unless the informant were killed there could be no peace afterward; the man was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changluan's daughter was married to Sihao's son. He memorialized that the report was slander meant to unsettle the nobles — that unless the informant were killed, trouble would follow. The man was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 思好旣誅，死者弟伏闕下訴求贈兄，長鸞不為通也。

translations.literal: After Sihao was put to death, the dead informant's younger brother prostrated himself below the palace gate, pleading that his brother be posthumously honored; Changluan would not relay the petition.
translations.idiomatic: After Sihao's death, the informant's younger brother lay prostrate below the palace gate, begging posthumous honors for his brother. Changluan refused to pass the petition.

sentences.zh: 平秦王歸彥，字仁英，神武族弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, courtesy name Renying, was a younger clansman of Shenwu on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, courtesy name Renying, was a younger cousin of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 父徽，魏末坐事當徙涼州，行至河、渭間，遇賊，以軍功得免流。

translations.literal: His father Hui, at the end of Wei, was implicated in a crime and sentenced to exile in Liangzhou; traveling between the Yellow and Wei rivers he encountered bandits and, through military merit, obtained release from banishment.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui, at the end of Wei, was implicated in a crime and condemned to exile in Liangzhou. Between the Yellow and Wei rivers he met bandits and, through military service, won release from banishment.

sentences.zh: 因於河州積年。

translations.literal: He therefore remained in Hezhou many years.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in Hezhou many years.

sentences.zh: 以解胡言，為西域大使，得胡師子來獻，以功得河東守。

translations.literal: Because he understood the Hu tongue, he served as ambassador to the Western Regions, obtained a Hu lion to present as tribute, and for merit was made Governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in the Hu tongue, he served as ambassador to the Western Regions, obtained a Hu lion to present as tribute, and was made governor of Hedong for his merit.

sentences.zh: 尋遂死焉。

translations.literal: Before long he died there.
translations.idiomatic: He died there not long after.

sentences.zh: 徽於神武舊恩甚篤。

translations.literal: Hui and Shenwu had been bound by deep old obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Gao Huan shared a deep old bond.

sentences.zh: 及神武平京洛，迎徽喪與穆同營葬。

translations.literal: When Shenwu pacified the capital and Luoyang, he brought Hui's coffin back and buried him in the same tomb precinct as Lady Mu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan pacified Luoyang, he brought Hui's coffin home and buried him in the same tomb compound as Lady Mu.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: Hui was posthumously made Minister over the Masses, posthumous name Wensuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister over the masses, posthumous name Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 初濟南自晉陽之鄴，楊愔宣勑，留從駕五千兵於西中，陰備非常。

translations.literal: At first, when the Prince of Jinan went from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin proclaimed the edict and left five thousand troops of the imperial escort in the Western Quarter, secretly preparing against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jinan first traveled from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin read the edict leaving five thousand troops of the escort in the Western Quarter — a secret guard against surprise.

sentences.zh: 至鄴數日，歸彥乃知之，由是陰怨楊、燕。

translations.literal: Several days after reaching Ye, Guiyan learned of it — and from this nursed secret resentment against Yang and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after reaching Ye, Guiyan learned of it and began to nurse secret resentment against Yang and Yan.

sentences.zh: 楊、燕等欲去二王，問計於歸彥。

translations.literal: Yang, Yan, and the rest wished to remove the two princes and asked Guiyan's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, Yan, and their faction meant to remove the two princes and sought Guiyan's counsel.

sentences.zh: 歸彥詐喜，請共元海量之。

translations.literal: Guiyan feigned delight and asked to take counsel together with Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan feigned enthusiasm and proposed consulting Yuanhai together.

sentences.zh: 元海亦口許心違，馳告長廣。

translations.literal: Yuanhai likewise assented with his mouth while his heart refused, and galloped to inform Prince of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai agreed with his lips while his heart refused, and raced to warn Prince of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 長廣於是誅楊、燕等。

translations.literal: Prince of Changguang thereupon put Yang, Yan, and the rest to death.
translations.idiomatic: Changguang thereupon executed Yang, Yan, and their allies.

sentences.zh: 孝昭將入雲龍門，都督成休寧列仗拒而不內，歸彥諭之，然後得入，進向柏閤、永巷亦如之。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao was about to enter the Cloud-Dragon Gate, Commander Cheng Xiuning drew up troops and barred him; Guiyan persuaded him, and only then was entry granted — proceeding toward the Cypress Pavilion and the Eternal Lane, the same again.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao was about to enter the Cloud-Dragon Gate, commander Cheng Xiuning drew up his troops and barred the way. Guiyan talked him round — only then was entry granted. The same at Cypress Pavilion and Eternal Lane.

sentences.zh: 孝昭踐祚，以此彌見優重，每入常在平原王段韶上。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao ascended the throne, for this he was all the more favored and honored — whenever he entered audience he was always ranked above Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao took the throne, Guiyan was favored all the more for this — at every audience he was seated above Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao.

sentences.zh: 以為司空，兼尚書令。

translations.literal: He was made Minister of Works and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of works and concurrently director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 齊制，宮內唯天子紗帽，臣下皆戎帽，特賜歸彥紗帽以寵之。

translations.literal: Under Qi law, within the palace only the Son of Heaven wore the gauze cap; all subjects wore military caps — Guiyan was specially granted a gauze cap as a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi law only the emperor wore the gauze cap within the palace; all others wore military caps. Guiyan alone was granted a gauze cap — a singular mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 孝昭崩，歸彥從晉陽迎武成於鄴。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao died, Guiyan went from Jinyang to welcome Wucheng at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao died, Guiyan went from Jinyang to welcome Wucheng to Ye.

sentences.zh: 及武成卽位，進位太傅，領司徒，常聽將私部曲三人帶刀入仗。

translations.literal: When Wucheng took the throne, Guiyan was advanced to Grand Tutor, held the title Minister over the Masses, and was regularly permitted to bring three private retainers, swords at belt, into the guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, Guiyan was made grand tutor and minister over the masses, and was regularly allowed three armed retainers at his side in the guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 從武成還都，諸貴戚等競要之，其所往處，一坐盡傾。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital with Wucheng, the high nobles all vied to invite him — wherever he went, the whole gathering leaned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital with Wucheng, the great families vied to host him. Wherever he went, the room tilted his way.

sentences.zh: 歸彥旣地居將相，志意盈滿，發言陵侮，旁若無人。

translations.literal: Guiyan now stood among generals and chancellors; his ambition brimmed over — his words were overbearing and insulting, as if no one else were present.
translations.idiomatic: Having reached the summit of general and chancellor, Guiyan's ambition brimmed over. His speech turned overbearing, as though no one else were in the room.

sentences.zh: 議者以威權震主，必為禍亂。

translations.literal: Commentators held that his might and authority alarmed the ruler — he would surely bring calamity and chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators warned that his power overshadowed the throne — disaster was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 上亦尋其前翻覆之跡，漸忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor also traced his earlier shifts of loyalty and gradually grew wary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, recalling his earlier betrayals, grew wary.

sentences.zh: 高元海、畢義雲、高乾乾和等咸數言其短。

translations.literal: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, Gao Qianhe, and others repeatedly spoke of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, Gao Qianhe, and others repeatedly denounced him.

sentences.zh: 上幸歸彥家，召魏收對御作詔草，欲加右丞相。

translations.literal: The emperor visited Guiyan's home, summoned Wei Shou to compose an edict in the royal presence, intending to add the title Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Guiyan's home and summoned Wei Shou to draft an edict in his presence — intending to add the title right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 收謂元海曰：「至尊以右丞相登位，今為歸彥威名太盛，故出之，豈可復加此號。

translations.literal: Shou said to Yuanhai: "His Majesty took the throne as right chancellor — now, because Guiyan's fame and power are too great, he is being sent out; how could that title be given again?
translations.idiomatic: Shou said to Yuanhai, "His Majesty took the throne as right chancellor. Guiyan's fame is too great — that is why he is being sent away. How can we give him that title again?

sentences.zh: 」乃拜太宰、冀州刺史，卽乾和繕寫。

translations.literal: " He was therefore appointed Grand Preceptor and Governor of Ji Province — Gao Qianhe copied it out at once.
translations.idiomatic: " Instead he was appointed grand preceptor and governor of Ji Province — Gao Qianhe copied the edict at once.

sentences.zh: 晝日，仍勑門司不聽輒入內。

translations.literal: That same day, an order was issued to the gate office forbidding entry into the palace without permission.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an order went to the gate office: no entry to the palace without leave.

sentences.zh: 時歸彥在家縱酒，經宿不知，至明欲參，至門知之，大驚而退。

translations.literal: Guiyan was at home drinking freely; he knew nothing until dawn. When he wished to attend audience and reached the gate and learned of it, he was greatly startled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan was at home drinking through the night and knew nothing. At dawn he set out for audience — reached the gate, learned what had happened, and fled back in alarm.

sentences.zh: 及通名謝，勑令早發，別賜錢帛、鼓吹、醫藥，事事周備。

translations.literal: When he announced himself to take leave, he was ordered to depart early; money, silk, musicians, and medicine were separately bestowed — every need provided.
translations.idiomatic: When he announced himself to take leave, he was told to depart at once. Money, silk, musicians, physicians — every comfort was provided.

sentences.zh: 又勑武職督將悉送至青陽宮，拜而退，莫敢共語。

translations.literal: Military officers and commanders were also ordered to escort him all the way to Qingyang Palace; they bowed and withdrew, none daring to speak with him together.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers were ordered to escort him to Qingyang Palace. They bowed and withdrew — none dared speak with him.

sentences.zh: 唯與趙郡王叡久語，時無聞者。

translations.literal: Only with Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui did he converse at length — at the time none overheard them.
translations.idiomatic: Only with Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui did he speak at length — and no one heard what passed.

sentences.zh: 至州，不自安，謀逆，欲待受調訖，班賜軍士，望車駕如晉陽，乘虛入鄴。

translations.literal: Reaching the province, he could not feel secure; he plotted rebellion — intending to wait until the transfer of authority was complete, distribute rewards to the soldiers, watch for the imperial carriage to go to Jinyang, and seize Ye while it was empty.
translations.idiomatic: At his province he could not rest easy. He plotted rebellion — waiting until his transfer was complete, rewarding the troops, watching for the emperor's journey to Jinyang, then seizing Ye while the capital lay open.

sentences.zh: 為其郎中令呂思禮所告，詔平原王段韶襲之。

translations.literal: He was denounced by his chief clerk of the prince's household Lü Sili; an edict ordered Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk Lü Sili denounced him. An edict ordered Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao to move against him.

sentences.zh: 歸彥舊於南境置私驛，聞軍將逼，報之，便嬰城拒守。

translations.literal: Guiyan had long maintained private relay stations on the southern border; hearing that troops were pressing near, he sent word ahead and immediately closed the city and defended it.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan had long kept private courier stations on the southern border. Hearing that troops were closing in, he sent word ahead and shut himself within the city walls.

sentences.zh: 先是，冀州長史宇文仲鸞、司馬李祖挹、別駕陳季璩、中從事房子弼、長樂郡守尉普興等疑歸彥有異，使連名密啟，歸彥追而獲之，遂收禁仲鸞等五人，仍並不從，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chief Clerk of Ji Province Yuwen Zhongluan, Administrator Li Zuyi, Aide Chen Jiqiong, Attendant Fang Zibi, and Administrator of Changle Commandery Wei Puxing and others had suspected Guiyan of disloyalty and jointly sent a secret memorial — Guiyan pursued and captured them, then imprisoned Zhongluan and the other five; they still would not submit, and all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ji Province chief clerk Yuwen Zhongluan, administrator Li Zuyi, aide Chen Jiqiong, attendant Fang Zibi, and Changle commandery administrator Wei Puxing had suspected Guiyan of treachery and sent a joint secret memorial. Guiyan pursued and captured them, imprisoned all five — and when they still refused to yield, killed them.

sentences.zh: 軍已逼城，歸彥登城大叫云：「孝昭皇帝初崩，六軍百萬衆悉由臣手，投身向鄴迎陛下，當時不反，今日豈有異心？

translations.literal: The army had already pressed the walls; Guiyan mounted the ramparts and shouted: "When Emperor Xiaozhao first died, the six armies and a million soldiers all passed through my hands — I threw myself into going to Ye to welcome Your Majesty; I did not rebel then — how could I harbor a different heart today?
translations.idiomatic: The army was at the walls. Guiyan mounted the ramparts and shouted, "When Emperor Xiaozhao died, a million soldiers passed through my hands. I raced to Ye to welcome Your Majesty — I did not rebel then. Why would my heart be different now?

sentences.zh: 正恨高元海、畢義雲、高乾和誑惑聖上，疾忌忠良。

translations.literal: I only resent Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, and Gao Qianhe for deceiving the sage ruler and envying and destroying the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: I resent only Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, and Gao Qianhe — they deceive the throne and destroy the loyal.

sentences.zh: 但為殺此三人，卽臨城自刎。

translations.literal: Kill these three men and I will come before the walls and cut my own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Kill these three and I will come before the walls and cut my own throat.

sentences.zh: 」其後城破，單騎北走，至交津見獲，鎖送鄴。

translations.literal: " Afterward the city fell; he fled north alone on horseback, reached Jiaojin, was captured, and was chained and sent to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: " The city fell. He fled north alone on horseback, was taken at Jiaojin, chained, and sent to Ye.

sentences.zh: 帝令趙郡王叡私問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor had Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui question him privately as to his reasons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui question him in private.

sentences.zh: 歸彥曰：「使黃頜小兒牽挽我，何可不反！

translations.literal: Guiyan said: "To let yellow-chinned boys drag me about — how could I not rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan said, "Yellow-chinned boys dragging me about — how could I not rebel!

sentences.zh: 」曰：「誰耶？

translations.literal: " He asked: "Who?
translations.idiomatic: " Rui asked, "Who?

sentences.zh: 」歸彥曰：「元海、乾和豈是朝廷老宿？

translations.literal: " Guiyan said: "Yuanhai and Qianhe — are they venerable elders of the court?
translations.idiomatic: " Guiyan said, "Yuanhai and Qianhe — are they venerable elders of the court?

sentences.zh: 如趙家老公時，又詎懷怨。

translations.literal: In the days of the Zhao family's old lord, would I have nursed resentment?
translations.idiomatic: In the days of the Zhao family's old lord, would I have nursed resentment?

sentences.zh: 」於是帝又使讓焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor then sent men to rebuke him further.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent men to rebuke him again.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「高元海受畢義雲宅，用作本州刺史，給後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: He replied: "Gao Yuanhai took Bi Yiyun's mansion and used it as his own provincial seat, and was given rear-guard musicians.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Gao Yuanhai took Bi Yiyun's mansion for his provincial seat and was given rear-guard musicians.

sentences.zh: 臣為藩王、太宰，仍不得鼓吹。

translations.literal: I am a frontier prince and grand preceptor — yet I still may not have musicians.
translations.idiomatic: I am a frontier prince and grand preceptor — and still I may not have musicians.

sentences.zh: 正殺元海、義雲而已。

translations.literal: I would kill only Yuanhai and Yiyun.
translations.idiomatic: I would kill only Yuanhai and Yiyun.

sentences.zh: 」上令都督劉桃枝牽入，歸彥猶作前語望活。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered Commander Liu Taozhi to drag him in; Guiyan still spoke as before, hoping to live.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered commander Liu Taozhi to drag him in. Guiyan still spoke as before, hoping to live.

sentences.zh: 帝命議其罪，皆云不可赦。

translations.literal: The emperor commanded that his crime be deliberated; all said he could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commanded deliberation on his crime. All agreed he could not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 乃載以露車，銜枚面縛，劉桃枝臨之以刃，擊鼓隨之，並子孫十五人皆棄市。

translations.literal: He was loaded onto an open cart, a gag in his mouth, face bound; Liu Taozhi held a blade over him, drums beating as they went — he and fifteen descendants were all executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He was loaded onto an open cart, gagged and bound. Liu Taozhi held a blade over him while drums beat along the route — he and fifteen descendants were all executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 贈仁州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Governor of Renzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Renzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏時山崩，得石角二，藏在武庫。

translations.literal: In Wei times a mountain collapsed and two stone horns were obtained, stored in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times a mountain collapsed and two stone horns were found and stored in the armory.

sentences.zh: 文宣入庫，賜從臣兵器，特以二石角與歸彥。

translations.literal: Wenxuan entered the storehouse to distribute weapons among his followers and specially gave the two stone horns to Guiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan entered the armory to distribute weapons among his followers and specially gave the two stone horns to Guiyan.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「爾事常山不得反，事長廣得反，反時，將此角嚇漢。

translations.literal: He said: "Serving Changshan you did not rebel; serving Changguang you rebelled — when you rebel, use these horns to frighten the Han.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Serving Changshan you did not rebel; serving Changguang you rebelled. When you rebel, use these horns to frighten the Han.

sentences.zh: 」歸彥額骨三道，著幘不安。

translations.literal: " Guiyan had three ridges on his forehead bone; wearing a headcloth he could not keep it in place.
translations.idiomatic: " Guiyan had three ridges on his brow; a headcloth would not sit straight on his skull.

sentences.zh: 文宣嘗見之，怒，使以馬鞭擊其額，血被面，曰：「爾反時當以此骨嚇漢。

translations.literal: Wenxuan once saw it and grew angry; he had him struck on the forehead with a horsewhip until blood covered his face, saying: "When you rebel you should use this bone to frighten the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan once saw it and grew angry. He had Guiyan struck on the brow with a horsewhip until blood covered his face, saying, "When you rebel you should use this bone to frighten the Han.

sentences.zh: 」其言反竟驗云。

translations.literal: " His words of rebellion were fulfilled in the end.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end his words of rebellion came true.

sentences.zh: 武興王普，字德廣，歸彥兄歸義之子也。

translations.literal: Prince Pu of Wuxing, courtesy name Deguang, was the son of Guiyan's elder brother Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pu of Wuxing, courtesy name Deguang, was the son of Guiyan's elder brother Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 性寬和有度量。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous, harmonious, and possessed of measure.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was generous, even-tempered, and possessed of measure.

sentences.zh: 九歲，歸彥自河州俱入洛，神武使與諸子同遊處。

translations.literal: At nine years of age, when Guiyan came from Hezhou into Luoyang together with him, Shenwu had him lodge and roam with his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: At nine, when Guiyan came from Hezhou into Luoyang with him, Gao Huan had him lodge and roam with his own sons.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封武興郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 武平二年，累遷司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuping he rose in succession to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuping he rose to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 六年，為豫州道行臺、尚書令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Field Headquarters of the Yuzhou Circuit and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made field headquarters of the Yuzhou circuit and director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後主奔鄴，就加太宰。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Pu was additionally made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Pu was additionally made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 周師逼，乃降。

translations.literal: When the Zhou armies pressed close, he thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of Zhou closed in, he yielded.

sentences.zh: 卒於長安。

translations.literal: He died at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 贈上開府、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Upper Opening Establishment and Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted an upper opening establishment and the governorship of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 長樂太守靈山，字景嵩，神武族弟也。

translations.literal: Lingshan, Governor of Changle, styled Jingsong, was a clansman younger brother of the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshan, Governor of Changle, styled Jingsong, was Gao Huan's clansman and younger brother.

sentences.zh: 從神武起兵信都，終於長樂太守。

translations.literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raising troops at Xindu, and ended as Governor of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan when arms were raised at Xindu and ended his life as Governor of Changle.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、司空，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General and Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Wensuan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand general and minister of works, with the posthumous title Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 子懿，卒於武平鎮將，無子，文宣帝以靈山從父兄齊州刺史建國子伏護為靈山後。

translations.literal: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan made Fuhu, son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's father's elder brother, successor to Lingshan's line.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan appointed Fuhu — son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's father's elder brother — to carry on Lingshan's line.

sentences.zh: 伏護，字臣援，粗有刀筆。

translations.literal: Fuhu, styled Chenyuan, had modest skill with brush and ledger.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhu, styled Chenyuan, had some modest skill with brush and ledger.

sentences.zh: 天統初，累遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiantong he was successively promoted to Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiantong he rose through promotion to gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 伏護歷事數朝，恒參機要，而性嗜酒，每多醉失，末路逾劇，乃至連日不食，事事酣酒，神識恍惚，遂以卒。

translations.literal: Fuhu served through several reigns and always took part in confidential affairs, yet by nature he craved wine; in drunkenness he often blundered, and in his last years the habit grew worse still — for days he would take no food, doing nothing but drink until his mind wandered and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhu served several reigns and always stood in the circle of confidential counsel, yet wine was his weakness; drunk, he often stumbled, and toward the end the failing worsened — days passed without a meal, every hour given to the cup until his mind grew dim and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 建國侯孫乂襲。

translations.literal: Yi, grandson of Marquis Jianguo, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, grandson of Marquis Jianguo, succeeded to the line.

sentences.zh: 乂少謹。

translations.literal: Yi in youth was careful and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yi was careful and restrained.

sentences.zh: 武平末，給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuping era he served as attendant gentleman at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，為太府少卿，坐事卒。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was Vice Director of the Grand Treasury; he died by reason of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he served as vice director of the grand treasury and died having been convicted of an offense.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
